# Island server rendering

<!-- predictable:capability={"authors":["runner"],"backlog":false,"covers":["src/runtime/server.ts","src/runtime/islands.ts"],"created":"","guidelines":[],"id":"SPEC-403","lastModified":"","lastVerified":"","proseDigest":"ec5d58ac5a5547a0","relatedSpecs":[]} -->
The server side of the island runtime (src/runtime/server.ts and src/runtime/islands.ts) turns design-system components into static HTML that the client runtime later hydrates. registryOf collects, from the modules it is given, every export whose name starts with a capital letter and whose value is a component (a function, or an object with $$typeof), keyed by its export name; other exports are left out. ISLAND_TAG is 'ds-island' and SLOT_TAG is 'ds-slot'. renderIsland(registry, {name, props, id, slots}) throws '540-ds: component "<name>" is not registered' when the registry has no component of that name; otherwise it renders the component with its revived props to HTML, with id as the prefix of every id the component generates with useId, and wraps that HTML as <ds-island data-c="<name>" data-id="<id>" data-p="<props as JSON>">, escaping &, " and < in those attributes. revive turns encoded props back into props: an object with a string $slot becomes a Slot rendered as <ds-slot data-s="<slot id>"> holding that slot's HTML, and renderIsland throws '540-ds: slot "<slot id>" has no HTML' when its slots have no entry for it; an object with a string $el becomes an element of that HTML tag when the name starts with a lowercase letter, otherwise of the registered component of that name, with its revived p as props, and revive throws '540-ds: component "<name>" is not registered; include its island' when no such component is registered; any other array, object or plain value is revived member by member and keeps its shape. renderStatic(element, id) renders an element the same way, with id as the prefix of its generated ids, without the island wrapper. renderToString(element, {identifierPrefix}) renders it with identifierPrefix as that prefix, or none when it is absent, and renderToStaticMarkup is the same function.

# Areas

- **Design System Library**: The published React component and token library that is the product of this repository.
  - **Tokens**: The design tokens such as breakpoints and color manifests that underlie the visual system.
  - **Foundations**: The reference pages showing color, type, spacing, and radius primitives behind the components.
  - **Atoms**: The smallest reusable interface pieces like buttons, text, images, and icons.
  - **Molecules**: Small composed components like cards, fields, menus, and section headers built from atoms.
  - **Organisms**: Larger composed building blocks such as slides, decks, charts, and timelines used to assemble full pieces.
  - **Charts**: The chart building blocks such as legends, scales, and data tables used by data visualization organisms.
  - **Templates**: Full page templates, such as the talk template, that arrange components into a finished piece.
  - **Runtime**: The client and server runtime that renders components, hydrates islands, and serves pages.
  - **App Shell**: The top level app entry and setup files that wire the library together for preview and rendering.
- **MCP Server**: A server that lets an AI agent query the 540 design system while it assembles a piece of content.
  - **MCP Tools**: The individual queries an agent can call, covering components, patterns, templates, tokens, rules, and images.
  - **MCP Transports**: The ways the server can be reached, over HTTP, stdio, or Firebase hosting.
  - **MCP Metadata**: The generated metadata and image catalog describing components, patterns, and tokens for the tools to read.
- **Build and Check Scripts**: The command line scripts that build, render, and validate the design system and its pieces.
  - **Piece Rendering**: The scripts that render a finished piece from the template and check its structure, spelling, and rules.
  - **Runtime Panel**: A debugging overlay panel used while checking rendered pieces at runtime.
